verses.gurmukhi: ਸੀਸੁ ਨਿਵਾਏ ਢੀਂਗੁਲੀ ਗਲਿ ਬੰਧੇ ਜਲੁ ਉਚਾ ਆਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: sees nivaae ddee(n)gulee gal ba(n)dhe jal uchaa aavai|

en.bdb: To get water from a stream or pond, the dhingali (a pole with a bucket one end and a fulcrum in the middle used for drawing water) is lowered by catching hold of its neck, i.e. it is humbled forcibly and does not go down of its own.

verses.gurmukhi: ਘੁਘੂ ਸੁਝੁ ਨ ਸੁਝਈ ਚਕਈ ਚੰਦੁ ਨ ਡਿਠਾ ਭਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: ghughoo sujh na sujhiee chakiee cha(n)dh na ddiThaa bhaavai|

en.bdb: The owl is not pleased on beholding the sun or chakavi; ruddy sheldrake, the moon.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਿੰਮਲ ਬਿਰਖੁ ਨ ਸਫਲੁ ਹੋਇ ਚੰਦਨ ਵਾਸੁ ਨ ਵਾਂਸਿ ਸਮਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: si(n)mal birakh na safal hoi cha(n)dhan vaas na vaa(n)s samaavai|

en.bdb: The silk cotton (simbal) tree yields no fruit and the bamboo grows near the sandal but is not perfumed thereby.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਪੈ ਦੁਧੁ ਪੀਆਲੀਐ ਤੁਮੇ ਦਾ ਕਉੜਤੁ ਨ ਜਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: sapai dhudh peeaaleeaai tume dhaa kauRat na jaavai|

en.bdb: Given milk to drink, a serpent does not part with its poison and the bitterness of the colocynth also does not depart.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਥਣਿ ਚੰਬੜਿ ਚਿਚੁੜੀ ਲੋਹੂ ਪੀਐ ਦੁਧੁ ਨ ਖਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: jiau than cha(n)baR chichuRee lohoo peeaai dhudh na khaavai|

en.bdb: The tick clings to the cow's udder but drinks blood instead of milk.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਭ ਅਵਗੁਣ ਮੈ ਤਨਿ ਵਸਨਿ ਗੁਣ ਕੀਤੇ ਅਵਗੁਣ ਨੋ ਧਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: sabh avagun mai tan vasan gun keete avagun no dhaavai|

en.bdb: All these demerits I have and if any one do me a favour, I return it with undesirable trait.
Garlic can never have the perfume of musk.
